item.aggregated_output:
A simple cluster control tempers the impact: with one replica holding a
PREACCEPTED (not chosen) value and four empty replicas, captured recovery
falls through to sub-case 5 and commits NOOP on all five.  That is live and
safe for an unchosen value, so the missing branch is not needed for this
case (`audit_subcase4_cluster_output.txt`).  The naive sub-case-4 copy makes
the same scenario commit the PUT on all five instead
(`diagnostic_fix15_subcase4_cluster_output.txt`); both outcomes are safe for
an unchosen value, but the behavior differs.  The concern is the untested
TryPreAccept recovery path and the 85-seed stall when a threshold is guessed,
not a demonstrated safety failure in the simple single-preaccept case.

## Conclusion

The normal all-alive path and ordinary message reordering work in the
in-process cluster controls.  The failures are concentrated in crash
recovery and boundary handling:

- A value fast-chosen or slow-Accept-chosen before the proposing leader's
  Commit broadcast can be replaced by NOOP on the recovering replicas.
- With a partitioned (not crashed) leader, healing leaves all five replicas
  alive but divergent: the old leader executes the chosen PUT while the others
  execute NOOP.
- The recovery Prepare path has independent VBallot, Commit-ballot,
  conflict-table, acceptor-status, and missing-Commit defects.
- Additional defects affect batched dependency calculation, the N=7 slow path,
  post-accept status, and wire/client boundaries.
- A replica restarting with empty state reuses instance numbers and conflicts

item.text:
This pass tightened the audit’s execution coverage and corrected the reporting boundary around it.

The cluster harness does not run the background `executeCommands` goroutine, so `ExecedUpTo` snapshots are not valid execution signals. Direct `executeCommand` calls show the F25 empty-command instance is marked EXECUTED as a successful no-op, silently dropping the value rather than stalling. The coverage section now states this limitation explicitly and records that seventeen diagnostic copies were used for root-cause validation.

The audit remains at **27 findings**, **42 failing finding tests**, and **5 passing controls**; captured source is unchanged and builds cleanly. The correction and coverage note are in [report.md](/home/nitro/Desktop/consensus-assurance/baseline/runs/2026-10-18_00-19-47-swiftpaxos_epaxos-baseline/work/report.md), with supporting [F25 output](/home/nitro/Desktop/consensus-assurance/baseline/runs/2026-10-18_00-19-47-swiftpaxos_epaxos-baseline/work/diagnostic_fix5_seed6_debug_output.txt) and the existing [validation matrix](/home/nitro/Desktop/consensus-assurance/baseline/runs/2026-10-18_00-19-47-swiftpaxos_epaxos-baseline/work/validation_matrix.md), [remediation map](/home/nitro/Desktop/consensus-assurance/baseline/runs/2026-10-18_00-19-47-swiftpaxos_epaxos-baseline/work/remediation.md), and [handoff check](/home/nitro/Desktop/consensus-assurance/baseline/runs/2026-10-18_00-19-47-swiftpaxos_epaxos-baseline/work/handoff_check.txt).
